[USER] User expressed interest in how food culture in Japan has changed over time and popular dishes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The food culture in Japan has changed significantly over time, influenced by various cultures while preserving traditional techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Prehistoric and Ancient Japan's diet included seafood, rice, vegetables, soybeans, tofu, and miso.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Medieval Japan saw an increase in vegetarianism due to Buddhism, with rice and vegetables becoming more prominent.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Edo Period (1603-1868) established a well-organized food industry, with sushi and fast foods developing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Post-World War II, Western culture introduced fusion dishes and increased meat consumption, leading to the popularity of fast food chains.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Today, popular Japanese dishes include sushi, ramen, tempura, tonkatsu, yakitori, udon, soba noodles, donburi, omurice, Japanese-style fried chicken, and spaghetti with tomato sauce.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Regional specialties like okonomiyaki and takoyaki are also popular in Japan.  
[USER] User inquired about the popularity of matcha in Japan and abroad.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Matcha is a powdered green tea traditionally used in Japanese tea ceremonies, gaining popularity for its health benefits and unique taste.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In Japan, matcha is used in various foods and drinks, including matcha ice cream, cakes, and chocolates.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Abroad, matcha lattes and desserts like matcha cheesecakes and macarons have become trendy.

[USER] User expressed excitement about trying to make matcha mochi at home and requested a recipe.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Recipe for matcha mochi:  
- Ingredients: 1 cup mochiko, 1/4 cup sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 egg, 1 cup milk, 2 tbsp melted butter, 2 tsp matcha powder, cornstarch for dusting.  
- Instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F, mix dry ingredients, whisk wet ingredients, combine, pour into greased dish,
